title: Per-model service contracts and regional contingency quota playbook
creator: Maya Singh
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, operationally actionable spec for per-model service contracts (SLO bundle + contingency quotas) that ties SLI definitions, regional contingency credits, and automatic failover/circuit-breaker policies into a single declarative artifact. This ticket produces a playbook and schema for the contract and a migration plan for 10 high-throughput endpoints. The ambition is to reduce cross-team ambiguity about when to failover, how to bill contingency use, and how to reclaim error budget. This work complements existing SLI taxonomy work but focuses on quota/credit mechanics and enforcement surface for multi-region deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical contract schema (JSON schema) that lists model SLOs (availability, p95 latency, request-quality SLI), default contingency credit bucket rules, and failover priorities
Implementation checklist for runtime guardrail mappings (circuit-breaker thresholds, quota check order, fallback model mapping) documented and linked
Migration plan with a pilot for three endpoints including metrics dashboard queries and alert rules
Runbook for manual override, error-budget reconciliation, and post-mortem checklist
Signoff from Product and SRE with acceptance criteria met and at least one canary executed in staging
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya S: Kickoff - synched with SRE and PM. We agreed to pursue a quota/credit model instead of trying to force identical SLOs across regions. PM asked us to surface tenant-visible contract fields for transparency.

2026-03-11 Liam C: Initial draft of schema posted to Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELI/pages/Model+Contracts. Key fields: slo_targets, contingency_buckets, failover_priority, eviction_policy. Feedback requested from Runtime and Billing.

2026-03-11 Priya K (SRE): Review note - prefer p99 for tail-sensitive chat routes; recommended separating request-quality SLI into 'semantic_failure_rate' and 'neutral_response_rate' rather than a single heuristic. Raised a telemetry gap for semantic_failure_rate (see telemetry TODO below).

2026-03-12 Elena R (PM): Product acceptance criteria updated — contingency use must be visible in Console and reflected in per-team monthly report. Added link to Console dashboard mock: https://drive.redwood.com/console/mock/contingency-view

2026-03-12 Liam C: Design decision: contingency credits are allocated per-model-version per-region and carry an 'emergency' flag for manual top-ups. Credits amortize over 24h windows. This avoids immediate global failover and preserves regional capacity for tenants with pinned variants.

2026-03-12 Miguel F (Runtime): Implementation note - runtime change required: quota precheck hook to run before model selection. PR skeleton created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/runtime/pull/3821

2026-03-13 Maya S: Added circuit-breaker calibration guidance: 5xx rate > 1% over 1m OR p95 latency breach for 2 consecutive 30s windows triggers soft-fallback. Hard-fallback occurs when emergency contingency exhausted. Documented escalation: notify SRE channel and create automatic incident if hard-fallback invoked.

2026-03-13 Liam C: Telemetry TODOs - add semantic_failure_rate instrumentation, augment existing request-tags with 'contract_id' so Console can attribute contingency consumption per customer. Filed ENG-886522 for telemetry work.

2026-03-13 Priya K (SRE): Concern - cross-region rebalancing during sustained load could cause oscillation. Proposed cooldown window of 10m per contract failover decision to prevent flip-flop. Added to playbook.
2026-03-13 Elena R (PM): UX feedback incorporated - Console should show remaining contingency credits and estimated time to depletion at current burn rate. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-13 Liam C: Next step - produce example contracts for 'chat-short' (latency-sensitive), 'completion-bulk' (throughput-sensitive), and 'embedding-service' (quality-sensitive). Plan to run canaries in staging on 2026-03-20.
Link references: Confluence model contracts page, runtime PR, Console mock (links above).
decision_log: Adopted quota/contingency credit model (not per-region identical SLOs) to allow regional capacity conservatism and graceful degradation
Contingency credits scoped per model-version per-region with 24h amortization and emergency manual top-up
Soft-fallback thresholds: 5xx rate > 1% over 1 minute OR p95 latency breach x2 -> soft fallback to cheaper/pinned variant
Hard-fallback policy: emergency contingency exhausted OR availability below 99.5% over 5m -> hard-fallback and incident creation
Cooldown window: 10 minutes between automated failover decisions to prevent oscillation
Contract_id will be injected into telemetry to enable per-contract billing and dashboarding
implementation_notes: Runtime changes: add pre-routing quota hook, contract-aware routing, and eviction priority queue
Telemetry changes: new metric 'contract_contingency_burn_rate' and tag 'contract_id' on requests
Console changes: contingency view (remaining credits, burn-rate, predicted depletion), per-contract alerts
Billing: plan for contingency reconciliation in monthly invoice; temporary line-item 'contingency usage' to be implemented by Finance
Security: contingency manual-topup action requires RBAC scope 'contract.admin' and audit log entry
risks: Oscillation risk across regions if cooldown not respected
Telemetry gaps (semantic failure instrumentation) could make request-quality SLI unreliable
Unclear UX semantics could cause customer confusion about 'emergency' credit use
Billing alignment needed - finance must approve contingency reconciliation model
